steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Experiments test cause-and-effect by manipulating the independent variable (IV) and measuring the dependent variable (DV) while controlling extraneous variables. Types: lab (high control, low ecological validity), field (natural setting, lower control), natural (IV not manipulated), quasi (pre-existing groups). | Key Fact: Observations record behaviour without manipulation. Naturalistic: in a natural setting with no intervention. Controlled: some variables regulated. Covert: participants unaware. Overt: participants aware. Participant: researcher joins the group. Non-participant: researcher observes from outside. | Key Fact: Correlations measure the relationship between two variables without establishing causation.
